title: Biomechanical and Tomographic Outcomes in Pediatric Keratoconus Treated with Conventional Epithelium-Off Corneal Collagen Cross-Linking

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) license, link https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

groups.description: Conventional Dresden epithelium-off CXL (about 9 mm manual de-epithelialization, riboflavin 0.1%-dextran 20% every 3 min for 30 min, UVA 3 mW/cm2 for 30 min, 5.4 J/cm2) for progressive keratoconus (Amsler-Krumeich stages I-IV, Kmax below 65 D) in patients aged 13-18 years; 28 eyes of 23 patients, all pediatric keratoconus eyes treated at the OCULENS Clinic, Cluj-Napoca, 2019-2023; prespecified visits at baseline, 6, 12 and 24 months. Procedure described as cross-linking only (no cataract surgery).

series.notes: Mean ± SD (Table 2 caption); unit logMAR (row label; Methods: BCVA recorded on the logMAR scale); repeated-measures analysis of the 28 eyes at every visit.

exclusions.reason: change column; the absolute series is used

exclusions.what: Late events after the 24-month window (retreatment, keratoplasty indication)
exclusions.reason: described only; no acuity is tabulated after 24 months

notes: UCVA, Kmax, SP-A1 and thinnest pachymetry (Table 2) and the Corvis ST and Pentacam indices (Table 3) are mentioned here only.
Three eyes were later retreated (about 3 years) and one patient later had an indication for keratoplasty, all after the 24-month window; the article keeps these eyes in the 24-month analysis.
Inclusion required the ability to comply with scheduled visits through 24 months; all 28 pediatric eyes treated at the centre in the period form the cohort.
Five patients contributed both eyes; the analysis is eye-based.
